title: (The death of Moses — the close of the Torah)

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses climbed Mount Nebo from the plains of Moab to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. There the Lord showed him the whole land — from Gilead to Dan, all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea, the Negev and the whole region from the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar." — Deut 34:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At the end of his long journey, Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and there God shows him the whole promised land spread out before him. From Gilead to the sea, from the north to the Negev, God let Moses see it all with his own eyes. There is such tenderness in this moment. Though Moses would not enter the land, God did not leave him without a gift. He gave His faithful servant a sweeping view of the promise he had spent forty years journeying toward.

Notice the grace in this. God could have simply told Moses he would not enter and left it there. Instead, He climbed the mountain with him, as it were, and showed him the fullness of what He had promised. Even in disappointment, God was kind to Moses.

There are seasons when we, too, see God's promises more than we fully possess them — when we glimpse what God is doing without yet holding it in our hands. This can be hard. But like Moses, we can trust that God is faithful, and that seeing the promise is itself a gift of His grace.

The writer of Hebrews tells us that the faithful of old "only saw them and welcomed them from a distance," longing for a better country (Heb 11:13-16). Moses saw the earthly land from afar, but he was destined for something far greater — the heavenly homeland with God Himself. And so are we. Whatever promises we glimpse from a distance now, in Christ we are journeying toward a homeland we will one day fully possess.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever had to trust God while only seeing His promise from a distance?
2. How does God's kindness to Moses on the mountain encourage me?
3. What does it mean to long for the "better country" God has prepared?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for Your kindness even in disappointment, and for the promises You let me glimpse. When I see from afar what I cannot yet hold, help me trust Your faithfulness and long for the homeland You have prepared in Christ. Amen.
